page: Microsoft Azure E32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs spanning 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 4.5 GHz. Hardware resources include 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Attached local storage provides 1888 GB across high-speed NVMe SSD media, while no hardware GPUs are present on this server type.

Instruction set features on the E32ads_v7 include AVX-512 extensions such as AVX512_VNNI and AVX512_BF16, along with hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives including AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. In standard benchmarks, single-threaded throughput shows high efficiency, achieving top-tier ranking in stress-ng single-core execution (3762.48) and single-threaded gzip compression (41.49 GB/sec). Multi-core testing via PassMark CPU scores reached 57284.51, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 101.24 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs manifest primarily in execution throughput under memory-bandwidth-bound and parameter-heavy compute scenarios. Large-model LLM generation (70B) drops to 2.46 tokens/sec, reflecting the absence of discrete GPU acceleration for sustained deep learning tasks. In contrast, smaller architectures benefit from available vector instructions, demonstrated by top-tier text generation on small 135M parameter models reaching 394.04 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high RAM allocation coupled with 1888 GB of local NVMe storage reduces external dependency overhead for low-latency scratch space. The E32ads_v7 delivers an effective platform for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory key-value caches like Redis, big data processing pipelines, and data analytics tasks requiring substantial memory footprints.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, backed by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Utilizing x86_64 architecture with 16 physical cores and 2 threads per core, the configuration offers an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation alongside 1888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. While lacking GPU acceleration, the system incorporates AVX-512 vector support and cryptographic instruction sets. Benchmark metrics show top-tier single-threaded performance in stress-ng and compression tasks, complemented by strong multi-core ratings in PassMark. Though less suited for heavy 70B parameter model execution due to reliance on CPU-only processing, the hardware balance between high RAM capacity and local NVMe storage provides strong resource density. This profile aligns with memory-heavy workloads, including in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, and analytical data transformation pipelines.
